split.title: A lease pays you a number. A year pays you what actually happened.
split.intro: Move the sliders in the hero and this redraws. The left bar in every month is what a fixed lease really puts in your account after the void, the agent and the repairs. The right bar is what the same unit makes with us.
split.introBold: The dark part is your floor. The bright part is your share.
split.againstPre: Against {lease} from a fixed lease on the same unit. That is
split.againstPost: , on an asset you already own.
split.versus: Fixed lease, after the year happens
split.floorLabel: Your floor, even in our worst year
split.floorNote: Paid on the first, full or empty. If we let the rooms badly, we earn nothing and you still clear the lease.
split.cta: Get this number for my unit
split.ctaNote: Two fields, then Marcus comes to you with the real version of this chart, worked out on your actual unit.
split.fine: Indicative, from median asking rents in your district and from how our own nineteen rooms actually perform. The real floor is agreed in writing after we walk the unit.

why.title: We are asking for the deal that is worse for us in a bad year.
why.p1: A fixed lease pays us to pay you as little as possible. We would quote low, hold your unit for three years and keep everything above the number. Every owner who has signed one has the same quiet suspicion, and the suspicion is usually correct.
why.p2: A share flips it. We earn nothing until your floor is paid and the running costs are covered. Empty rooms come out of our side first. There is no version of this where we do well and you do not.
why.p3: That is the whole argument. Not that we are nicer, but that we have deliberately taken the structure where the only way we make money in year two is to keep your unit full in year one.

trial.title: Ninety days, then decide.
trial.body: We spend our money before you spend yours. We furnish the unit, shoot it, list it across every channel and start paying your floor, all before anything binds you to us. At day ninety you carry on or you walk.
trial.bodyTail: We take our furniture back out at our own cost and leave the unit as we found it.
trial.zero4: To walk away at day ninety

keep3.k: Our list of what the unit needs
keep3.v: Yours, even if you say no

trial.string1: Anyone we house during the trial signs a real lease, because they are real people moving their lives into your unit. So if you leave at day ninety you pick how that lands: take the tenancies over as they stand, with the agreements and the deposits handed to you, or give us the time to see them out.
trial.string2: That is the whole of the small print. We would rather put it on the page than bury it in a clause you find in month four.

stay.head: Never short-let
stay.body: Every tenancy is written at three months or longer, inside the URA rule for private homes. No nightly stays, no exceptions, no letter from the authorities.

occ.head: Inside the cap
occ.body: We let to the occupancy limit for your property type and write that limit into the agreement, so an extra body cannot quietly appear.

data.head: PDPA, and GDPR
data.body: Tenant identity documents are collected once, stored encrypted, masked in the portal, and deleted on schedule. Our tenants come from Europe too, so we hold to GDPR as well.

stamp.head: IRAS, by us
stamp.body: Every agreement is stamped, and we do the stamping for tenants who have no Singapore bank account yet. The certificate sits in your portal.

hive.title: What we've learned running the houses.
hive.body: Everything we pick up running nineteen rooms across three condos ends up here. What a Singapore unit actually earns once the empty month is counted, what the URA rules mean on a Tuesday rather than in a circular, what breaks in year two and what it costs to fix. No lead magnets and no gated PDFs.

reach.title: Your rooms go on sale in places you have never heard of.
reach.body: A room in Serangoon gets taken from Chengdu, Bangalore or Berlin, weeks before the tenant lands in Singapore. We list, price and sync every room from one system, so a booking on any channel closes the others in the same minute. An agent puts your unit on two portals and waits for a phone call.

catch.q: What is the catch with the ninety days?
catch.a: That we spend real money on your unit before you owe us anything, and we are betting you will not want to unwind it once you have watched it run. That is the bet, and it is on our side of the table. The only string is the tenancies: anyone we house signs a real lease, so at day ninety you either take those over as they stand or give us the time to see them out.

empty.q: What if the rooms sit empty?
empty.a: Then you are paid the floor and we are paid nothing. The floor is the first call on the money, ahead of our costs and well ahead of our margin. That is the point of the structure, and it is why we will not quote a floor before we have seen the unit.

lease.q: So the floor is just a lease with extra steps?
lease.a: In a bad year, yes, and deliberately so. The difference shows up in a normal year, when a lease would have kept the whole upside on our side of the table and this does not.

furniture.a: We do, at our cost, to one standard across every home. You put in nothing. At the end of the term the unit comes back the way we found it, or better, with the condition written down and photographed on day one.

see.q: Can I actually see what is happening?
see.a: Yes, from the day you sign, and you can see most of it on this page already. Every booking, every rate, every payout line, the tenant documents, the maintenance log and the inspection photos. Not a quarterly PDF.

back.q: What if I want the unit back?
back.a: There is a notice period and it is in the agreement before you sign. We will not hold your asset hostage. What we ask is enough notice to see out the tenancies already signed, because those are real people with leases.

eligible.a: Private condominiums and apartments, let at three months or longer, within the occupancy cap. HDB flats do not work for this model and we will say so rather than waste your afternoon.

arrears.q: Who deals with a tenant who stops paying?
arrears.a: We do, and it does not touch your floor. You will read about it in the arrears log if you want to. You will not be asked to do anything about it.

comb.title: Every room on the map is real.
comb.introPre: Nineteen rooms so far, each one drawn where it actually stands on the island.
comb.introTail: and you get the room itself, straight from the same database that runs the booking site: the photographs, the price, the size, the bed, what is in it and when it next opens. The pale shapes are the rest of Singapore, the part we have not built yet.
comb.hint: Click a filled room to open the listing

ask.kicker: The next step is a coffee
ask.p1: Not a call. Not a deck. Tell me roughly where your unit is and I will come to you, anywhere on the island, at whatever hour suits. I will buy the coffee, look at the photos on your phone, and tell you what I think your unit would actually make.
ask.p2: If it is not a fit I will say so before the cup is cold, and you will have lost forty minutes and gained a flat white.
ask.saved: Saved. This is what Marcus brings to the table.
ask.attached: Everything you worked out on this page is attached to your enquiry, so the first thing he says is not "tell me about your unit".
ask.variantPre: Your enquiry is saved against hero variant
ask.variantPost: which is how we find out which opening line actually produces coffees. Marcus is messaged within a day.
ask.whatHappens: What happens when you press that

wh1.b: Marcus messages you on WhatsApp to pick a time and a place. Your place, your office, the coffee shop downstairs, whichever is least effort for you.

wh2.b: No slides and no laptop. He brings a printed one page read on your unit, worked out from what you have entered here plus what the district is actually renting for.

wh3.b: Whether you go ahead or not. If your unit is not a fit he will say so at the table rather than send you a polite email next week.

ask.signFine: Marcus · Makery Pte Ltd · the one who actually turns up
ask.noSpam: No newsletter. No sequence of five emails. No agent ringing you on a Sunday.

ref.faq: Questions that come up every week
ref.walkTimes: Walk times are in each property panel.

q1.a: Yes, with advance notice to the housemates. Three nights or more needs approval from us first.

q2.a: Fibre broadband at every property, 300Mbps or better, and coverage reaches every room.

q3.a: Yes, the shared kitchen is fully equipped. Clean up after, and use the exhaust fan for anything heavily spiced.

q4.q: How do they report a problem?
q4.a: A ticket in the tenant portal, or a WhatsApp message to the SG line. We aim to reply inside 24 hours.

q5.a: One month of written notice. The deposit may be forfeited depending on the circumstances, so check before promising.

q6.q: When does the deposit come back?
q6.a: Within 14 days of move-out, after the room inspection. Deductions only for damage beyond fair wear.

q7.a: Water, electricity with a monthly AC allowance, WiFi and weekly common cleaning are all in the rent. AC above the allowance is billed at cost.

q8.a: HDB parking near Chiltern Park and Ivory Heights. Thomson Grove has limited porch parking. Check before committing.

q9.a: Smart plugs meter each room against its monthly allowance, and any overage is billed the following month.

q10.q: How much notice does a viewing need?
q10.a: Two working days, minimum. A captain has to be lined up to open the unit, so never offer same day or next day.

greet.welcome: This is the Lazybee room desk. Live availability, pricing and open dates for all 19 rooms, straight from the same database the booking site reads.

what.title: What this is
what.body: Every room across our three homes in Singapore, with live pricing and the date each one frees up. It reads the same database the public booking site does, so what you see here is what a tenant is quoted.

search.title: Searching
search.body: Give it a move-in date and a budget and it shows what fits. Flexible widens the date by a month. Budget is a ceiling with a little stretch, so cheaper rooms always show.

card.title: Reading a room
card.body: Tap any room to open it. Inside are photos you can save, the full specification, what comes with the room, and a 3D tour where one exists.

badges.title: The availability badge
badges.body: Open now means it is empty today. A date means it frees up then. Occupied to a date means somebody is in it until then. Anything opening within twelve weeks is worth actively selling.

ladder.title: Price by lease length
ladder.body: Twelve months is the anchor and the price we push. Shorter costs more per month, longer costs less. Quote from the ladder rather than negotiating your own number.
